transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-07-19 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Rohan Iyer (GlobalMedix), Sofia Martinez (GlobalMedix), Ellen Chu (Security), Tom Alvarez (Product)

Summary:
Short scoping call to agree POC success criteria and model shortlist for a multilingual clinical QA proof-of-concept. Discussed dataset size, latency and accuracy targets, hosting options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and a 1-week benchmark sprint plan. Action items and timelines agreed.

Topics:
- Success criteria (exact match, value-based, hallucination tolerance)
- Workload sizing and expected qps / tokens
- Benchmark plan + metrics and tooling
- Model shortlist + quality/latency tradeoffs (multilingual clinical domain)
- Security/compliance: data residency, KMS, audit logs
- Timeline: 4-week pilot, immediate 1-week bench sprint

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone good afternoon, um thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Rohan: hi i'm rohan, i lead ai at globalmedix. we've been looking to replace a brittle rules system for clinical question answering across english, spanish, and portuguese.
[00:16] Maya: perfect thanks rohan. carlos and leah from our SE team will run through sizing and benchmarks. carlos over to you.
[00:23] Carlos: awesome. so high level: we want to decide the model shortlist and the test harness. what are your main success criteria for the poc? is it exact-match, F1, or user-satisfaction?
[00:33] Tom: product wants high precision, like exact-match for fact retrieval when the question is about medication dosing — false positives are bad. but for explanatory answers we can tolerate some variation if there's a confidence score.
[00:45] Sofia: and add multilingual parity — spanish and portuguese are first-class. we need >85% EM-ish in english and within 5-7 points in other languages.
[00:55] Maya: okay that helps. any latency requirements? p95 targets?
[01:00] Rohan: ideally p95 under 300 ms for single-turn queries. we understand batch tradeoffs but realtime UX expects snappy replies.
[01:08] Carlos: noted. that pushes towards smaller/highly-optimized variants or quantized weights. we discussed earlier 8-bit and 4-bit int quant profiles; 4-bit can help cost but may degrade answer fidelity on clinical jargon.
[01:22] Ellen: on security: we need SOC2 type II evidence, KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency in eu-us split. also SSO for engineers.
[01:34] Leah: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem, but for the bench sprint we can run in Hosted with strict retention and a contract NDA; if POC looks good we can pivot to Dedicated or Private.
[01:46] Sofia: do you have existing benchmarks for clinical QA? we're worried off-the-shelf metrics like rouge won't capture hallucinations.
[01:54] Carlos: agree. we'll run both EM and a hallucination metric — we'll surface answer provenance/confidence and use targeted red-team prompts. plan: automated EM + manual review for a random sample of 100 cases per language.
[02:07] Tom: sizing — expected qps? we have spikes during clinician shift changes. average 5 qps, peak 25 qps. payloads small: ~80-150 tokens per request, responses ~30-200 tokens depending on detail.
[02:23] Carlos: ok using those numbers, for hosted with Redwood autoscaling we estimate single-region baseline of 2 gpus provisioned for stable latencies; Dedicated reserved for steady 25 qps — we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[02:34] Rohan: cost target — we want to keep inference cost under $0.01 per session at scale.
[02:39] Maya: we will produce cost estimates for three configs: hosted burst, dedicated reserved, private with customer infra.
[02:46] Sofia: model shortlist? what are you proposing for multilingual clinical quality?
[02:50] Carlos: shortlist we recommend: (1) Mosaic-X-13B quant 8/4 profiles (good balance latency/quality), (2) Llama-3-20B-instruct variants for high quality but heavier & costlier, (3) Mistral-Med fine-tuned candidate (if available) — Mistral tends to be strong on instruction following but less proven in clinical text. Also consider fast small models for routing — e.g., 7B distilled for simple lookups.
[03:14] Rohan: any concerns about hallucination with the 4-bit quant?
[03:17] Carlos: yes — sometimes factual recall degrades with aggressive quant; we'll benchmark exact-match on gold QA set and review answer confidence. for the bench sprint we'll compare full fp16 runs vs 8-bit and 4-bit runs.
[03:29] Leah: note: KV cache behavior matters for multi-turn context; our runtime optimizes cache reuse across turns to reduce latency. might be relevant for follow-up clarifications.
[03:40] Ellen: on compliance — will logs contain PHI? we need guidance on PII scrubbing and retention.
[03:47] Maya: yes we recommend anonymizing data for benchmarking. Redwood can enable log redaction and short retention for Hosted POC; Private gives you full control. we'll document options.
[03:58] Tom: timeline — what's realistic?
[04:00] Carlos: propose immediate: share spreadsheet + harness (this week), customer uploads data by Fri, Redwood runs 1-week bench sprint Mon-Fri next week, results review + decision meeting the following week. overall pilot (if green) 4 weeks to validate and then expand.
[04:14] Rohan: that fits. who owns the bench harness?
[04:17] Maya: Redwood will spin up the harness; we'll provide instructions for dataset formatting and a pre-seeded repo. you'll get collaborator access.
[04:25] Sofia: any tooling for automated evaluation across languages?
[04:28] Carlos: yes we'll use the same harness that supports EM, BLEU-ish signals, and our hallucination detector. we'll also attach human review workflow for the manual sample.
[04:39] Ellen: encryption keys — can we BYOK?
[04:42] Leah: yes for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports KMS integration with customer-managed keys in some regions. we'll note region constraints.
[04:51] Maya: ok quick recap of success criteria: 1) EM >= 85% english, within 5-7 points spanish/portuguese; 2) p95 latency <300 ms for single-query; 3) hallucination rate <5% on reviewed samples; 4) cost per session in target band; and 5) security checklist satisfied (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence).
[05:10] Rohan: sounds good. one question — competitors: we ran a small pilot with Luminai and Anthropic — they had good quality but cost was higher and latency inconsistent. curious how Redwood compares on consistency.
[05:22] Carlos: our routing/fallbacks help maintain consistency; we'll show you p95 variability charts from similar workloads.
[05:31] Tom: last bit — what about model updates mid-POC? we need stable baselines.
[05:36] Maya: we'll pin model versions and snapshot everything; any updates will be explicit and part of the benchmark notes.
[05:42] Rohan: ok if we agree to timeline, next step is to receive the harness link and cost table.
[05:47] Maya: agreed. i'll share benchmark spreadsheet and our recommended shortlist and runbook by end of day tomorrow. carlos will provision the project.
[05:54] Sofia: thanks all.
[05:56] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and a calendar invite for the bench sprint kickoff.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: some technical terms may be slightly off: e.g., KMS sometimes transcribed as "K M S", model names shortened, and mild speaker overlap between tom and sofiya at times.
